text: Beyond the open window, bamboo brushes bamboo. A few dry sounds reach the room, with long pauses between. On the sill, a moth has folded its wings.
mutation_dimensions: replace conceptual sound description with literal auditory intervals
hypothesis: A concrete account of pauses may retain the settling sound pattern while reducing attention to the writer. This is an editorial hypothesis, not a measured improvement.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates A10; slight self-consciousness in spaces belonging to the room

text: Beyond the open window, bamboo brushes bamboo. The sound is slight enough that the spaces between it belong to the room. On the sill, a moth draws its wings close and is still.
mutation_dimensions: replace completed resting pose with a small motion ending in stillness
hypothesis: Allowing the moth to settle during the final sentence may give the existing bamboo intervals a visible stopping place; it may also be less economical than the parent.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates A10; folded moth as final resting body

text: The greenhouse glass is clouded at the corners. Inside, the leaves overlap in every shade of green. Water stands in the lip of a clay saucer. A drop falls from the pot above it. The surface becomes smooth before the next.
mutation_dimensions: split the final sentence into a fall and a recovery interval
hypothesis: Separate sentences may let the reading pace follow one drop and the water settling, while preserving the greenhouse scene and recurrence. The shorter cadence could also feel clipped.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates E08; duration between drops

text: The greenhouse glass is clouded at the corners. Inside, the leaves overlap in every shade of green. Water stands in the lip of a clay saucer. Beneath the pot's drain hole, a bead grows, lets go, and dimples the water. The small rings fade before another falls.
mutation_dimensions: make the water source and formation of each drop physically explicit
replace general smoothness with the fading of visible rings
hypothesis: The bead forming before release may express slowness more precisely than a slowly falling drop, and fading rings may make the return to stillness easier to picture. Added detail may cost simplicity.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates E08; interval and physical coherence findings

text: The brushes rested in a jar of clean water. A little blue loosened from the bristles. It spread through the jar until there was no edge to it.
mutation_dimensions: replace the person finishing work with a still-life opening
hypothesis: Beginning with brushes already resting may reduce chore-related attention and bring the blue diffusion forward. Removing the afternoon may lose some warmth.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates D09; small narratives can be busier

text: At the end of the afternoon, he put the brushes in a jar of clean water. A little blue loosened from the bristles. It drifted through the clear water, growing paler as it spread.
mutation_dimensions: replace loss of a color boundary with gradual fading of the blue
hypothesis: Following a color becoming paler may offer a more continuous sensory taper than stating that its edge disappears. The original boundary image may be more distinctive.
evidence_reference: literary-review-one.md: Promising candidates D09; color losing its edge
